links.outcome: Sensitivity of ML model versus ASQ screening on same data for suicide attempt/death within 90 days
links.effect: ML medium-risk threshold sensitivity 0.782 (95% CI 0.648-0.915) vs ASQ alone 0.178 (95% CI 0.073-0.282); NPV 0.999 vs 0.997.
links.quote: The ML model outperformed ASQ screening on sensitivity and NPV at the evaluated thresholds; however, because the model included prior screening and ideation features, this comparison reflects the incremental value of longitudinal EHR information rather than a contemporaneous head-to-head assessment of the index screening alone.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of ML plus screening in parallel (ML as adjunct) versus screening alone
links.effect: Parallel ASQ or ML medium/high risk sensitivity 0.795 (95% CI 0.671-0.920) vs ASQ alone 0.178, without missing any cases caught by screening; PPV 0.012.
links.quote: Instead, parallel testing brings immediate value to the field by preserving universal screening and allowing ML to act as a clinical “safety net” to identify at-risk patients who are missed by current practices.

links.outcome: Reliance on ML dependent on prior EHR history; patients with sparse data and missing screening
links.effect: 37.3% (16,019/42,915) of ED visits lacked documented ASQ screening; ML requires longitudinal data, so patients new to the system have minimal data for prediction.
links.quote: Patients with limited or no prior health care encounters—such as those new to the system or seeking care for the first time—would have minimal data for the algorithm to analyze.

links.outcome: Predictive values at local prevalence for suicide risk identification
links.effect: At 0.4% outcome prevalence, PPVs were low (0.012-0.050) despite reasonable sensitivity/specificity; NPV 0.997-0.999.
links.quote: The PPVs we observed (0.012-0.050) reflect the mathematical reality that low prevalence constrains PPV even when sensitivity and specificity are reasonable, a challenge inherent to predicting any rare outcome.

links.outcome: ASQ sensitivity in local American Indian population lacking validation
links.effect: ASQ sensitivity was only 0.178; 41 of 55 (74.5%) patients with outcome never screened ASQ positive; no suicide death was ASQ positive.
links.quote: Our findings, showing a sensitivity of only 0.178, suggest that the tool may perform differently in this population or that implementation challenges limit effectiveness.

links.effect: Parallel ASQ or ML ≥75th percentile: sensitivity 0.795, specificity 0.742; ASQ alone sensitivity 0.178, specificity 0.970.
links.quote: Parallel testing strategies, where patients were flagged if they were screened as positive or were classified as at risk by the ML model, substantially improved sensitivity compared to screening alone.

links.effect: ML ≥75th percentile sensitivity 0.782, NPV 0.999 vs ASQ sensitivity 0.178, NPV 0.997.
links.quote: The ML model outperformed ASQ screening on sensitivity and NPV at the evaluated thresholds; however, because the model included prior screening and ideation features, this comparison reflects the incremental value of longitudinal EHR information rather than a contemporaneous head-to-head assessment of the index screening alone.

links.effect: Serial high-risk ML AND ASQ: PPV 0.050 vs ASQ 0.022, but sensitivity 0.129 vs 0.178.
links.quote: Third, serial testing requiring both positive ML classification and positive screening achieved more than a 2-fold improvement in PPV (0.050 vs 0.022) but with reduced sensitivity (0.129 vs 0.178).
